finding: Over 17 NBA seasons, lateral ankle sprains were the most frequent injury (1,658 cases, 13.2%), while patellofemoral inflammation cost the most games (10,370 games, 17.5%).
source_title: Drakos et al., Injury in the NBA: a 17-year overview

finding: 2013-14 to 2016-17: 796 sprains, about a 25.8% chance per player per season. Roughly 71% involved contact and 80% were lateral. A sprain in the prior year raised incidence 1.41x.
source_title: Ankle sprains in the NBA, 2013-14 through 2016-17 (abstract)

finding: In a randomized trial of 1,460 high school players, braced players had 0.47 acute ankle injuries per 1,000 exposures vs 1.41 for controls. Braces reduced how often injuries happened but not how severe they were.
source_title: McGuine et al., lace-up ankle braces in high school basketball (summary)

finding: A 22-week pilot trial of a sport-specific balance program (5-10 min, 3x/week) found a 0.30 relative risk of lateral ankle sprains vs controls. The sample was small and the intervals were wide.
source_title: Sport-specific balance training and ankle sprains in basketball (abstract)

finding: Video of 38 NBA ACL tears (2006-2022): about 76% indirect contact and 24% non-contact, none from a direct blow to the knee. Knee valgus rose from 5.1° to 12.0° within 33 ms of foot strike. Most common situations: first step toward the basket, landing after mid-air contact, jump stop.
source_title: Video analysis of ACL tears in NBA players (abstract)

finding: 8 of 9 active NBA players returned to NBA play, at a mean of 9.8 months. PER fell in the first season back (12.5 to 7.6) and was no longer significantly lower by the second season.
source_title: Return to sport after ACL reconstruction in NBA players (abstract)

finding: Of 27 NBA ruptures, 81.5% were non-contact and 74% occurred during take-off or acceleration, with forefoot loading and the ankle snapping into about 42° of dorsiflexion. Authors suggest eccentric calf work, lumbopelvic and knee stability, and forefoot acceleration training.
source_title: Achilles ruptures in NBA players: sequential video analysis (abstract)

finding: 44 NBA ruptures, 1969-2018: all filmed cases were non-contact push-offs. 36.8% of players never returned or started fewer than 10 more games, and 21% retired. Mean return was 10.5 months.
source_title: Epidemiology and video analysis of Achilles ruptures in the NBA (abstract)

finding: About 80% of 25 surgically treated players returned, after about 311 days. Two seasons later VORP was down 24.1% and offensive rating was significantly lower.
source_title: Return to play and performance after Achilles rupture in the NBA (abstract)

finding: In 19 ruptures (2014-15 to 2024-25), players averaged 29.0 min in the 10 games before injury vs 27.4 the rest of the season. The authors stress this does not prove workload is a cause (no control group).
source_title: Short-term workload before Achilles rupture in NBA players (2026)

topic: Calf strain as a warning sign
finding: A 2026 retrospective study specifically examines prior calf strain as a risk factor for Achilles rupture in NBA players. Durant (2019) and Haliburton (2025) both ruptured soon after a same-leg calf strain.
source_title: Prior calf strain as a risk factor for Achilles rupture in NBA players (2026)

finding: The commissioner reported seven Achilles injuries in 2024-25 vs none the season before and said the league convened an expert panel. He floated using AI on game video to look for patterns.
source_title: Malay Mail / wire report on the NBA's Achilles review

finding: Across 15 studies (8,459 athletes), programs including the Nordic hamstring exercise had a risk ratio of 0.49 for hamstring injury, about a 51% reduction.
source_title: van Dyk et al., BJSM meta-analysis

finding: 76 lower-extremity bony stress injuries in NBA players (2005-2015): 55% in the foot, half within the first 6 weeks of the season. 42.9% of players with a fifth-metatarsal stress fracture did not return to pro play. Surgery outperformed non-operative care at 2 years.
source_title: Lower extremity stress injuries in professional basketball (abstract)

finding: A cluster-randomized trial found a short Copenhagen adductor strengthening program prevented groin problems in male football players.
source_title: Harøy et al., The Adductor Strengthening Programme (BJSM 2019)

finding: Across 681 game injuries (2012-13 to 2014-15), back-to-backs and 4-in-5 stretches were not associated with a higher game-injury rate on their own. Away games were.
source_title: Game injuries in relation to game schedules in the NBA (abstract)

finding: The condensed 2020 schedule had 1.42x the injury proportion of 2015-2018, excluding COVID absences, and 1.67x for players averaging 30+ minutes.
source_title: Effect of a condensed NBA season on injury risk (abstract)

finding: Only healthy players keep logging heavy minutes, so naive models make recent workload look protective. Correcting for this pushes estimates back toward load increasing risk.
